word_order: SVO | English in the sample uses Subject–Verb–Object (e.g. 'The game (S) is based (V) on the Second Battle (O)'; 'Arthur Guinness signed (V) a 9,000 year lease (O)').
register: edited written prose — encyclopedic / Wikipedia-style and newsy factual sentences (formal, well-formed clauses rather than spontaneous speech).
target_transfer_hazards: parenthetical acronym patterns like '(' followed by an abbreviation then ')'
notes_for_prompt_writer: This source is formal, well-formed English: most sentences are complete clauses, so waiting to close a clause costs little naturalness. For German, avoid emitting segments immediately after subordinators or relative pronouns (the items listed under unstable_prefix_signals/target_transfer_hazards) because German moves the finite verb to the clause end and translation choices (word order, tense/auxiliary placement) remain unsettled until the subordinate/relative clause finishes. Treat appositives, 'called/named', lists after 'such as/including', and parenthetical acronyms as non-boundaries — do not split there. Prefer splitting after the end of main clauses or at coordinating conjunctions only when the main clause is complete.

target_language_profile.word_order: Main clauses: V2 (S V O); subordinate and relative clauses: verb-final. DP internal order is fairly rigid; adverbials/fronting can vary (pairs 12, 6, 18, 1).
target_language_profile.verb_placement: Finite verb appears second in main clauses; in subordinate/relative/infinitival contexts the verb/participle/particle appears clause-final — force deferring finite verb and particle output (pairs 12, 6, 11, 18).
late_commitment_forced_by: separable particles / phrasal-verb particles (e.g., zurück, hinunter) (pairs 12, 2)
case/gender for articles and adjective endings (pairs 1, 9, 3)
relative/subordinate clause boundaries that change word order (pairs 6, 11)
target_language_profile.reordering_vs_source: German often defers verbs/particles to clause end, places complements before final verbs, and attaches relative clauses post-nominal, causing long-distance reordering (pairs 11, 6, 12, 18).
safe_boundary_signals: closing comma that ends a subordinate/relative clause in source (pair 6, 11)
a following finite verb or conjunction, signalling prior NP ended (pair 12)
unsafe_boundary_signals: before a subordinate/relative marker ('that','which','although','who') — verb-final may be required (pairs 6, 18)
before the English phrasal verb particle appears ('back','away','down') — separable particle placement unknown (pairs 12, 2)
before the head noun appears to determine gender/case for articles/adjectives (pairs 1, 9)
